mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPI YoY > 2.5%, or if the correlation between CPI YoY and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE decreases > 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS increases for 3 months, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO decreases > 2% MoM, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at a rate above 2% year-over-year, the combined effect of tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressures leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when both conditions are met, or if the combined effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases by > 200,000, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a surge in demand for new homes, which boosts related industries and increases economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 10% MoM, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is declining and Real GDP (GDPC1) is growing, this divergence signals a supply-side constraint that can lead to inflationary pressures and reduced profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both conditions are met, or if the combined effect of INDPRO decline and GDPC1 growth on 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
